speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport what considerations have been put in place to ensure that Singaporean taxi and private hire drivers' livelihoods are safeguarded even if more licences are made available to Malaysian cross-border services upon review of the Cross Border Taxi Scheme.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry is looking into facilitating more point-to-point (P2P) transfers between Singapore and Johor Bahru given the setting up of Johor-Singapore Economic Zone; and (b) if so, how will the Ministry safeguard the livelihood of Singapore P2P drivers given the large cost disparity of driving Malaysian-registered and Singapore-registered vehicles.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has been conducting enforcement operations against illegal point-to-point (P2P) services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We recognise that there is demand from commuters for more convenient cross-border P2P services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) and LTA have been exploring options to enhance the existing arrangements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will provide greater convenience to commuters from both countries.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To minimise foreign taxis cruising around empty and potentially carrying out illegal trips, these foreign taxis would only be allowed to pick up passengers at designated points so that they do not infringe into the local P2P market.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, for the convenience of commuters, we will identify more pick-up points in both Johor Bahru and Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will discuss options with the Malaysian authorities on a reciprocal basis.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: LTA will continue its enforcement efforts even after enhancements to the existing arrangements are rolled out.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I declare I am the adviser to NTA and NPHVA.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Given the deep social and economic ties between Singapore and Malaysia, our drivers have expressed through the associations that they are excited that the calls to review and update the current Cross Border Taxi Scheme are being looked into.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: With the programme being updated, and I have taken note of the Senior Minister of State's response, with the increasing demands for P2P drop-offs, how will the Ministry use technology such as online booking platforms and in-vehicle tracking units to ensure that there is fair competition between Singapore-licensed and Malaysian-licensed vehicles, noting that there are fare and exchange rate differences?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Also, more importantly, how will the Ministry look to expanding the scheme to allow our drivers broader earning opportunities?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, there is a lot of unmet demand from commuters who would like to travel more frequently across the border.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have families with children, families with the elderly, families who want to visit relatives in Johor Bahru.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, it is under these conditions that we are looking at how to enhance the current Cross Border Taxi Scheme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member had some questions with regard to the use of technology.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We see that some of our taxi operators have already rolled out online booking forms, phone calls as well, to facilitate doorstep pick-up in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, I have shared that we can make use of the installation of the on-board unit (OBU), especially on foreign taxis, in order to enhance location tracking.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And not to forget our platform operators, the ride-hail platform operators, also have technology platforms that they can use to enhance location tracking.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, these are ways in which we can ensure that foreign vehicles are not conducting illegal P2P trips in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The second question she had was with regard to fares.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When it comes to fares, we will have discussions with the NTA as well as the NPHVA to understand what are the reasonable fares we should be looking at to enhance cross-border trips.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We know that there are cost disparities between the cost of operating as well as driving in Singapore versus Johor Bahru, so, we will take this into consideration when setting fares.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Before I go on, let me declare I am the CEO of Strides Premier, a company that provides cross-border taxi service as well.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: First of all, what is the plan that LTA has to expand the fleet of 200 cross-border taxis to more, and whether it will allow the application by a taxi driver on a monthly basis, rather than restrict it to once a year?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Because private hire cars' pricings are quite dynamic and as pointed out by the Senior Minister of State, the operating cost of driving a P2P vehicle in Johor Bahru is a small fraction of what is the cost in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: So, how would MOT consider measures to prevent the undercutting of fares in this matter?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member had a second question with regard to private hire vehicles.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This, I would approach cautiously because we have been having discussions with our local NPHVA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They are conscious that if we should liberalise the Cross Border Taxi Scheme too widely and not have a separate scheme for private hire vehicles, there could be a situation where private hire vehicles could end up providing illegal P2P services in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think what is important to note is that any vehicle, especially those which are foreign that operate in Singapore, they need to have the necessary decals, the necessary livery, so that is very clear that they are part of a licence scheme that has been negotiated between both countries, and not individuals owning private hire vehicles conducting illegal P2P trips.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Yes, could I ask him to repeat that?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Yes, thank you to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: My third question is that we know the cost of operating a taxi in Malaysia is a small fraction of the cost of operating a taxi in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But that said, it is very important that we enforce effectively.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And that is why I have emphasised the need for us to have the installation of the OBU, for instance, for the purposes of location tracking and also discussing with platform operators to use their technology platforms to track where the vehicles are going.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: I note that Senior Minister of State had in her reply talked about working with ride-hail platforms, and I also have reports of ride-hail platforms from across the border being set up, introducing cross-border taxi services.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: How will LTA or MOT be working with these overseas registered apps to ensure that there is parity and fairness when it comes to offering such rides in Singapore as well as in Malaysia?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Such apps have to be recognised by both Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, where we are aware that there are apps that are being used to provide cross-border services, but have actually not been endorsed by our local authorities before-hand, we will investigate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We cannot allow the proliferation of apps that have not been discussed between both authorities before.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is to ensure that there will not be illegal P2P trips being conducted via such apps.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I have asked a question on how could we prevent the undercutting of fares, because the cost of operating a taxi in Malaysia is only a fraction of the cost of operating a taxi in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think what the Member is concerned about is rides that are illegal, and the fares of these illegal rides are undercutting the fares and the services that are being provided by legal provision of such services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, for such illegal provision of services where fares are undercutting the fares that are pre-negotiated between both countries' authorities, we will enforce in a strict manner against such illegal providers of services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may build on the question by Ms Yeo earlier on, I have also received feedback from residents engaged in private hire vehicle services that these illegal ride-hailing services are offered not just via unauthorised apps, but also via chat groups.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My first question is I am wondering whether the Ministry has a sense of the pervasiveness of such illegal services being offered via chat groups as well as apps.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And secondly, if the Ministry has a plan to crack down on such means of securing services, for example, using "secret shopper" or methodologies of this nature?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Under Singapore's laws, the Government can order the take down of content linked to illegal activities and non-compliance can lead to further enforcement actions like blocking access or app removal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, this is with regards to illegal chat groups that promote the provision of illegal P2P services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MOT and LTA are also looking to obtain further legal powers to ensure that online platforms comply with LTA's removal request for illegal P2P services should the platforms remain unresponsive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, the LTA has also been conducting operations to infiltrate into these chat groups and to take action against providers of such illegal services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Unfortunately, for operational reasons, I cannot share more details.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But rest assured that LTA is aware of the situation.
